metadata.description: Canonical static rules, preprocess recipe truth, production targets, and facility templates for Arknights: Endfield. Certified runtime still consumes frozen data/preprocessed artifacts.

emptiness_adjudication.statement: No occupant of any kind may intersect the target empty rectangle: facility bodies, power poles, belts, cross-junction/bridge components and every other logistics part are forbidden. 'Empty' means completely clear ground; the earlier permissive reading that admitted routing components inside the rectangle is void.

semantics._note: Descriptive, machine-anchored clarifications for external review / proof-audience alignment. NOT consumed by the demand solver, instance builder, placement generator, or any certified solve path. Editing keys here changes only this file's frozen hash (freeze-ritual), never the derived preprocess artifacts. Predicate IDs refer to the 6 CERTIFIED predicates in PROJECT_LOCK.md.

axiom_kernel.role: The game-semantics axioms below are the semantic ground for this semantics section: the other entries are theorems or owner rulings OVER this kernel and carry axiom_derivation annotations pointing back here. Like the whole semantics section this entry is descriptive only, never consumed by any solve path. No axiom changes any certified predicate; the 6 predicates remain connectivity/geometry-only.
axiom_kernel.scope_premises: Game v1.1 valley-4. Upstream baselines are TWO DIFFERENT repositories, not one: JamboChen/endfield-calc@8da9017a (2026-07-17) is the recipe/item/facility numeric catalog and carries NO geometry; hsyhhssyy/IndustrialPlanner@dd334ed5 (2026-07-17) is the base-placement simulator supplying entity geometry, ports, base definition and logistics devices (attribution source: docs/research/rules_audit_20260718/00_owner_adjudications_and_rule_corrections.md section 1; an earlier canonical wording put both commits under one repository name and is corrected here). Current simulator audit baseline: IndustrialPlanner@7b946c16 (2026-08-05) - every simulator-side cross-check from 2026-08-05 onward was run against it. Player configuration that defines the initial instance, including warehouse-item links and any player-set slot locks relied upon by a claim, is allowed before execution starts and is treated as frozen initial state. After execution starts, all permanent-blocking and non-self-healing conclusions assume no player intervention, including the documented manual clearing or reset actions. Claims about any other runtime reconfiguration require separate adjudication. Authority order: owner in-game adjudication > simulator rule layer > canonical text > document paraphrase.

axioms.A1_transport_conservation: On inter-device transport edges items are neither created, destroyed nor moved backwards; creation/destruction happens only inside device recipes (A9) and at network boundaries (warehouse pickup chains per A11; submission into the warehouse). Default failure mode of a transport step: the move simply does not happen and the item waits upstream in place (owner-confirmed simulator-equivalent; earlier 'bounce-back' wording was terminological only, not reverse transport). Known exceptions: explicitly configured per-device blockage auto-clearing (destroys items; unconfigured it is fully inert), waiting-output blocking (item stays inside the producing device), partial warehouse submission.
axioms.A2_content_filter_points: Exactly four game-rule content tests are recognized in this scope: (i) admission rules at the deliberately unmodeled 1x1 admission port; (ii) cache-slot typing and static slot locks under A3; (iii) pipe-family domain locks, which are inapplicable to this all-solid project under A10; and (iv) item-domain flags and player-configured warehouse or slot links under A11. Sender-side scheduling is content-blind: splitter rotation reads priority groups and cursors, never item identity. Receiver-side arbitration may nevertheless be effectively content-selective when one upstream node exposes multiple readable slots, because it tries sources according to whether their current item can pass the applicable landing tests above; this does not create a fifth content rule. A2 alone does NOT make that multi-slot case unreachable. In the frozen facility universe, a separate topology theorem follows from A5(a) plus the single-slot-per-channel parameters: every in-use machine input is reached through one aligned single-slot transport channel on its front cell, so receiver arbitration has no alternative source slot on that machine-input edge. Bare machine intake remains recipe-blind: an item that can land in a compatible cache slot is accepted regardless of the selected recipe; an item that cannot yet land waits upstream under A1. Instant item-id rejection exists only at admission ports. The admission port itself is deliberately not modeled - see item_admission_port_exclusion.
axioms.A3_cache_slots: Cache-slot typing is a two-regime system: dynamic typing (the first item pins an empty slot's type; count reaching 0 clears it) and static locks (compile-time warehouse slot pre-locks and manual player locks; never released by emptying). One commodity per slot at any time. An empty slot accepts any domain-matching commodity not already held by another slot of the same slot GROUP; a full same-type slot rejects at node level rather than overflowing to a free slot. Group = storageSlotGroup = one solver node; in-group exclusion does not cross groups (the protocol storage box is 6 independent single-slot groups, so the same commodity may occupy several of them).
axioms.A4_device_composition: A logistics-participating device = ports + cache-slot groups + behavior rules acting on its BOUND slot set, which may be proxied to other devices' slots (share-all chains, warehouse sink). The warehouse is the unique implicit per-base device: one compile-time pre-locked slot per commodity type, capacity 2^53-1 (finite but practically unreachable). The wired warehouse INPUT side is the protocol core alone (warehouse-sink rewrite of the landing slot; non-rejecting for any commodity already registered with a warehouse slot). Boundary storage ports are 0-in/1-out warehouse PICKUP ports whose output commodity is player-configured (A11). The protocol storage box is NOT a warehouse-line port: no connection, box-to-warehouse wireless submission only, machine mechanics otherwise, and it requires power (A8).
axioms.A5_interfaces: (a) The only inter-device interface through ports is port-to-front-cell; the stored port coordinate in candidate placements IS the front/belt cell itself (zmd convention; the simulator's inside/outside two-point model converts only via the single _port_front_cell helper). Exactly three non-port pathways exist: box-to-warehouse wireless submission, warehouse-sink landing rewrite, dark-pipe share-all cross-distance link. Zero-gap machine-to-machine interfacing is impossible - a theorem over (a), not an axiom. (b) An unconnected port is legally idle and claims no front cell. (c) The outermost ring is fully functional; bodies may touch the edge and each other; belts cannot leave the 70x70 grid. (d) FrontUsable: a front cell is blocked if and only if a facility body occupies it (power poles included); belts do not block; perpendicular straight cross-transit through the cell is legal (both parties straight).
axioms.A6_form: (a) Owner form axiom: every logistics device laid on the grid is a specialized straight belt; functional belts are straight-only; one cell never hosts two independent devices (dark pipe = explicit off-grid exception). The cross junction is ONE single-cell device with two mutually perpendicular internal channels which may carry different commodities. (b) Belts are single-channel FIFO with no overtaking (simulator single-slot parameter makes it trivially true; game-side multi-item FIFO untested - this half-clause is not owner-attributed).
axioms.A7_rates: Belt line throughput cap = 30 items/min (tick 2.0 s, belt capacity 1 item per tick), aggregated across commodities; 2 s headway between consecutive items. Device cadence upper bound = recipe duration (attained absent blocking and starvation). Admission filtering only ever reduces long-run flow. Rates never enter the certified predicates; any certification-narrative use of rate arithmetic must go through semantics.rate_lemma_scope. Rate-to-geometry conversion is fixed at the single point slots = ceil(rate/cap) into integer port counts; per manufacturing slot parameters (one input buffer slot x 50 per ingredient, all same-side ports bound to one buffer group) this conversion is a demand-side lane lower bound and direction-safe.
axioms.A8_power: The hub (protocol core) is the base's power source; poles draw from it unconditionally at any distance and are the only coverage broadcasters, active immediately on placement; coverage = 12x12 axis-aligned stencil per pole with the INTERSECTION criterion (at least one body cell covered); power budget externalized to another base. Power is a behavioral PRECONDITION, not an orthogonal annex: an uncovered powered device performs none of its behavior rules - e.g. an unpowered storage box never flushes, so its occupied slots never clear.
axioms.A9_transformation: Device processing is defined by recipes: it consumes exactly the declared input set, produces exactly the declared output set, at cadence = duration; this is the only in-device creation/destruction point (complementing A1's edge conservation). Recipe sets are built into machines - players cannot author recipe content, one machine generally carries several recipes, and processing starts when cached inputs match ANY recipe of the set (owner 2026-08-06). Intake is recipe-blind while processing is recipe-exact; that gap is the entire pollution mechanism: a wrong item that matches another recipe of the set gets processed into wrong products polluting downstream, and one that matches none has no consumption channel and occupies its slot permanently. Output side: when products cannot be placed the recipe halts in waiting-output, the device blocks, no product is destroyed (simulator answer taken as working default; game-side undecided).
axioms.A10_domains: Items carry Solid/Liquid/Gas domain flags; slots, ports and pipe families filter by domain; pipe families additionally carry connected-component domain locks. Project scope rests solely on: all 19 commodities are solid and belt-carried, so pipe constants, pipe phase gating and component domain locks are inapplicable (scope, not nonexistence).
axioms.A11_commodity_identity: Source-side commodity identity comes from player configuration: what a boundary pickup port or core output emits is set by per-slot warehouse-item links (share-all chains to the warehouse's typed slots) - a special case of A2 filter point (iv). The binding model's assignment of one commodity per boundary-port generic_output slot mirrors this axiom. Legal initial state: map crops provide the first seeds (owner-adjudicated); the general legality domain of pre-seeded caches remains unadjudicated (adjacent question, separate clause).

axiom_kernel.ruling_level_inputs: Two clauses of this file are owner rulings NOT derivable from the kernel (adjudication-level inputs): empty-rectangle strictness (globals.empty_rectangle.emptiness_adjudication; kernel derivation #14) and warehouse_bridge_exclusion (kernel derivation #15; conditional on the frozen production targets).
axiom_kernel.model_stricter_faces: Registered faces where the certified model is STRICTER than adjudicated game semantics. Feasibility direction: provided the remaining model is faithful, a model-feasible layout is still game-feasible, so these restrictions do not create false-positive feasibility claims. Optimality direction: no such safety follows automatically. For the max_lex objective, the restricted-model optimum is at most the adjudicated-game optimum in lexicographic order. A full-game optimality claim is sound only when every excluded face is either part of an explicit certification-scope restriction or covered by a separately verified without-loss-of-generality/completeness proof. Otherwise the certificate proves optimality only over the restricted model domain. Registered faces: (1) ROUTING-LAYER destination-front single-commodity exclusivity (the routing model's sink-front exclusivity, imposed on the front CELL of a receiving port) must be split by terminal class. Its application to class (3) machine inputs is the adjudicated pollution-safety encoding (kernel derivation #8a) and is not, by itself, a model-stricter debt. Its application to class (1) protocol-core inputs, and to any class (2) storage-box input execution that satisfies the class-(2) acceptance invariant, is model-stricter; (2) source-front single-commodity exclusivity is a confirmed over-strict face because output-door transit is owner-adjudicated safe (owner 2026-08-06); any unlock remains a separate sealed-face batch, deliberately NOT part of this freeze-ritual; (3) routing reverification adds no-orphan and selected-source-reaches-sink conditions beyond the adjudicated connectivity quantifier; (4) BINDING-LAYER slot single-commodity typing - a different layer from (1), which constrains the front CELL: this one constrains the port SLOT itself, every binding slot carrying exactly one commodity although adjudicated wired warehouse-line inputs may absorb several commodities at once (see port_commodity_scope for the scope declaration this creates); (5) warehouse_bridge_exclusion removes a real game wiring structure and is justified only by its separately stated, target-conditional production-line argument. Until that argument is formalized as a completeness proof, full-game optimality must treat it as an explicit scope restriction; (6) ITEM-ADMISSION-PORT OMISSION: the 1x1 filtering admission port exists in game v1.1 and is deliberately not modeled. Because its item-filtering behavior can change the operational safety of a mixed route, omitting it may remove an adjudicated-game behavior, and this batch accordingly downgrades that omission from an unconditional safe-exclusion theorem to an explicit certification-scope restriction (see item_admission_port_exclusion). This entry is the debt record required by model_stricter_faces_completeness. Disposition owner-decided 2026-08-07 - keep the omission in place - carried on four terms: the de-mix prohibition stays unconditional for now but may no longer cite item_admission_port_exclusion as its justification; this ledger entry is the registered debt; evidence is to be gathered by extending the existing diagnostic arm rather than by modeling the filter cell; and the exclusion's authority lapses the moment such a predicate is wired into the released model (see item_admission_port_exclusion.authority). Reopen triggers: that predicate landing, or the first wall-audit round, in which this face is the named seed case.
axiom_kernel.model_stricter_faces_usage_rule: This registry is a model-debt and certification-scope ledger, not a source of game-semantic premises. A registered stricter face may be cited to describe the current restricted model, but it must not be used to prove a theorem about adjudicated game semantics or to support a full-game lex-optimality claim. Any current-model theorem that depends on a registered face must name that dependency and is invalidated for re-proof when the face is unlocked. Unlocking a face changes the modeled domain and requires the affected solve, bounds and certificate narrative to be regenerated.
axiom_kernel.model_stricter_faces_completeness: This ledger is required to be exhaustive for every model restriction known to remove an adjudicated-game behavior. Absence from the ledger is not evidence of equivalence. Each newly discovered face must be registered before it is used in a certified solve or optimality narrative.

boundary_placement.statement: The left/bottom boundary lane INCLUDES the (0,0) corner: both the left-baseline vertical poses and the bottom-baseline horizontal poses admit the corner anchor. The candidate domain enumerates all such poses and MUST NOT pre-delete mutually-exclusive corner poses during generation; mutual exclusion is enforced downstream by cell-exclusivity in the master, not by pruning the candidate pool.
boundary_placement.axiom_derivation: kernel A5b (an unconnected port is legally idle and claims no front cell - the owner ruling that forbade whole-side out-of-grid pruning) + A5c (the outermost ring is fully functional; bodies may sit on it). See semantics.axiom_kernel.

routing_cross_junction.statement: The 'elevated'/L1 and 'ground'/L0 layers are a MODELING representation of a single-cell cross-junction component (two mutually perpendicular straight through-channels sharing one cell). There is no physical ramp, elevation, or layer transition. The two channels may carry DIFFERENT commodities but must be perpendicular when co-located; a bridge cannot turn (can_turn=false) and cannot host a non-straight component on the same cell.
routing_cross_junction.clarifies: The prior 'elevated bridge' wording was read literally as a 3D ramp; it is not.
routing_cross_junction.axiom_derivation: kernel A6a (owner form axiom: functional belts straight-only, no two independent devices per cell; the cross junction is ONE single-cell device with two perpendicular internal channels - can_overlap_straight_belt=true is that single device's modeling representation, not a second belt on the cell) => derivation #11 (no turning bridge, no bridge over curved / splitter / merger cells). See semantics.axiom_kernel.

mixed_commodity_flow.statement: A single physical belt / routing component may be SHARED by multiple commodities. Commodity mixing on one component is allowed. Throughput / bandwidth / discrete capacity remain OUT-OF-SCOPE (PROJECT_LOCK.md 1A B): the certified predicates constrain connectivity and geometry only, not flow volume.

terminal_clause.adjudicated: 2026-08-06 owner port-semantics final adjudication + precision fix (archived: docs/research/canonical_batch_20260807/PORT_SEMANTICS_REVERDICT_A_20260806.md, appendices one and two). For receiving-terminal scope this canonical clause supersedes any archived wording that includes boundary_storage_port among absorbing terminals, on two independent grounds: (a) port orientation - preprocess_plan fixes boundary_io at 0 generic input slots and 1 generic output slot, so it has no physical input port at which a receiving branch could terminate; (b) cell count (2026-08-07 reasoning closure ordered by owner - a DERIVATION over the frozen instance, not an in-game adjudication) - boundary-line devices fit only the left-plus-bottom edge strip of 139 cells (70 + 70 - 1 shared corner), of which the mandatory set already consumes 46 boundary pickup ports x 3 cells = 138, so a second boundary-line device class (the simulator's 3x1 storage-side loader with one WarehouseSink input) would need 141 > 139 cells and cannot be placed in ANY layout holding the 266 mandatory instances. This cell-count leg is CONDITIONAL on a stated premise set - change a premise and it must be re-derived: (i) the frozen production targets, which fix the pickup-port count at 46; (ii) the storage-side loader obeying the same left_or_bottom_boundary rule as the pickup port - owner-tested 2026-07-18 for the pickup half, but EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE SIMULATOR (same tag, same bus-attachment rule) for the storage half, NOT owner-adjudicated; (iii) a 3x1 port body; (iv) the 70x70 grid. It re-derives on any production-target change - the same trigger as warehouse_bridge_exclusion.
terminal_clause.statement: This tri-partition ranges only over modeled physical RECEIVING facility input ports at which a belt segment terminates. Output-only ports and devices with no physical input port are outside the partition. In particular, boundary_storage_port is a 0-input/1-output warehouse pickup source and is NOT a class (1) terminal. The statement above remains true at BELT level: belts and cross-junction channels legally carry interleaved commodities (owner in-game test; kernel derivation #9). It was however adjudicated TOO WIDE at PORT level - whether a mixed segment may legally TERMINATE somewhere depends on the destination's port class. Adjudicated tri-partition: (1) WIRED warehouse-line input ports - the protocol core's 14 physical inputs, the only wired warehouse input side - absorb any mix of warehouse-registered commodities without rejection (per-commodity warehouse slots, capacity practically unreachable); (2) the protocol storage box is a BOUNDED mixed absorber - see protocol_storage_box_wireless.slot_count_clause: 6 independent single-slot cache groups, one commodity per occupied slot, the same commodity may occupy several slots, and, for an arrival of a commodity that no slot already holds with remaining capacity, the box blocks when all 6 slots are occupied REGARDLESS of how many commodity types are involved (slot-count wording is deliberate; the earlier type-count reading was the too-wide mistake this clause closes); occupied is not the same as full - see protocol_storage_box_wireless.slot_count_clause for the per-arrival acceptance invariant that governs class-(2) safety; (3) machine input ports have NO content selectivity (intake is recipe-blind, kernel A9): a non-recipe item that lands in a cache slot has no consumption channel and occupies it permanently (transport conservation + no return, kernel A1), so mixed flow terminating at a machine input port is unsafe. Terminal clause: a mixed-commodity segment is unconditionally safe by terminal class only at class (1). It may terminate at class (2) only when a separate execution argument establishes the per-arrival acceptance invariant stated in protocol_storage_box_wireless.slot_count_clause; class (2) membership, or a count of commodity types, does not itself discharge that invariant. For THIS frozen instance the invariant is nevertheless discharged, by owner adjudication 2026-08-07 (project ledger docs/项目说明/00_master_roadmap.md, 2026-08-07 box ruling): 3 input ports x 1 item per 2 s across the 10 s flush period admit at most 15 arrivals per cycle; 15 is far below the box's 300-item static capacity and below even a single slot's 50; pure-flow commodity kinds are at most 3 against 6 groups - see protocol_storage_box_wireless.slot_count_clause.blocking_reachability_note for the model dependence of that count; and every cycle clears. The 6-occupied blocking state is therefore physically unreachable in this instance - the sole theoretical route to it, a mixed belt carrying 7 or more kinds inside one 10 s window, cannot be assembled here because the only commodities reaching the storage line are the 2 final products - and even a transient stall would clear within 10 s and can never poison the box. The protocol storage box is accordingly a legal mixed-flow terminal in this instance. This is an INSTANCE-LEVEL discharge recorded against the frozen 266-instance set, not a change to the class-level rule stated above: any other layout must discharge the invariant on its own. Mixed flow terminating at class (3) remains unsafe under the pollution premises stated above, and the certified model's sink-front single-commodity exclusivity is a correct conservative encoding of that class (3) case. The rate lemma narrows the mixing domain to final-product terminal segments only for a particular layout that separately discharges every precondition in semantics.rate_lemma_scope. The certified predicates do not discharge those preconditions, so this terminal clause makes no unconditional claim that all other legal layouts are intermediate-pure-flow.
terminal_clause.axiom_derivation: Pollution-chain derivation: kernel A5(a) plus the frozen single-slot-per-transport-channel device parameters make the immediate machine-input transport edge single-source at any instant; A2 supplies sender-side content blindness and the receiver arbitration rule; A3 supplies dynamic slot typing and finite landing capacity; A9 supplies recipe-blind intake and recipe-exact consumption; A1 supplies waiting with no reverse transport or spontaneous destruction. These premises together, not A2 alone, yield derivation #1 for class (3). Any use of sorting-terminal derivation #21 is subject to this corrected receiving-terminal universe: among the modeled utility facilities, protocol-core inputs are structurally non-rejecting receivers; boundary_storage_port is output-only and cannot terminate a receiving branch; the protocol storage box is only conditionally accepting under its separately stated cache invariant. See semantics.axiom_kernel.

connectivity_quantifier.statement: Predicate 5 ('routing connectivity') means: per commodity, every SINK front is reachable from SOME source front AND every SOURCE front can reach SOME sink front. Multiple independent connected islands of the same commodity are ALLOWED. It is NOT a single-spanning-component requirement and NOT a throughput guarantee.
connectivity_quantifier.axiom_derivation: kernel derivation #16: edge conservation (A1) + steady-state premise => every source front needs a destination and every sink front a source; 'multiple islands allowed' is the absence of any forbidding clause, fixed by owner ruling 2026-07-02. The certified model is registered as STRICTER than this quantifier (conservative): sink-front single-commodity exclusivity, and the routing reverification's additional no-orphan / selected-source-reaches-sink conditions. See semantics.axiom_kernel (model_stricter_faces).

machine_min_clearance.statement: machine_min_clearance_cells is NOT one of the 6 CERTIFIED predicates. Adjudicated meaning (re-adjudicated 2026-07-18, front-offset incident, owner in-game tests: zero-gap dead / one-gap routes / a 1-cell belt is legal / two opposite ports may share the middle cell): the stored port coordinate in candidate placements IS the front/belt cell itself — the first cell outside the facility body along the outward normal; an in-use port requires THAT cell to accept a belt, i.e. it must be in-grid and not occupied by any facility body (power poles count as body and block; belts do NOT block — belt/belt co-location on the front cell is governed solely by routing_cross_junction: perpendicular straight channels may cross, a turning or parallel same-axis foreign belt blocks the port). Enforced via identity front-cell modeling — NOT as 'port + direction offset' (the pre-2026-07-18 one-cell-offset misreading that checked the second cell outside the body), and NOT as a generic N-cell moat around every machine body. Machine bodies may touch; there is no body-to-body clearance requirement. Repeated external reviews misread it as body-clearance; it is not.
machine_min_clearance.adjudication_ref: PROJECT_LOCK.md B-4 + F-RT-R2-01/R3-01 + F-FRONT-INC-01; incident file docs/research/front_offset_incident_20260718/00_incident_survey_and_fix_plan.md
machine_min_clearance.axiom_derivation: kernel A5a (stored port coordinate IS the front cell - zmd candidate-pool convention; the simulator's inside/outside two-point model converts only via the single _port_front_cell helper; the front-offset incident is this axiom's counterexample history) + A5d (FrontUsable closed set: blocked iff facility body, poles included; belts do not block; perpendicular straight transit legal) => derivation #10 (zero-gap machine-to-machine interfacing impossible - a theorem, not an axiom). See semantics.axiom_kernel.

warehouse_bridge_exclusion.statement: The in-game 'warehouse bridge' (any commodity submitted to the warehouse via protocol storage box or hub inputs can physically re-emerge from hub outputs AND boundary pickup ports) is REAL game mechanics but is EXCLUDED as a legal wiring structure in this model: re-emitting intermediates crowds the output capacity of blue-iron/source ore, whose output rates directly bound final-product throughput, making the bridge non-viable under the 3.0/2.75-line production targets. Therefore the direct-connection connectivity model (every intermediate commodity must be belt-routed from a producer port to a consumer port; the warehouse is not a routing shortcut) is the adjudicated modeling choice. If the production targets ever change, this exclusion must be re-adjudicated.
warehouse_bridge_exclusion.authority: owner production-line argument; upstream simulators model the bridge and cannot adjudicate viability
warehouse_bridge_exclusion.axiom_derivation: NOT derivable from the axiom kernel - adjudication-level input (kernel derivation #15): a modeling choice bound to the frozen 3.0/2.75 production targets; must be re-adjudicated if the targets change, as already stated above. See semantics.axiom_kernel (ruling_level_inputs).

protocol_storage_box_wireless.statement: The protocol storage box has REAL physical ports identical in shape to manufacturing_3x3 (3 inputs on one side, 3 outputs on the opposite side, four orientation modes) and requires power. The 'wireless' segment exists ONLY from box to warehouse: with power and its default-on switch, the box flushes its 6 cache slots into the warehouse every 10s. Products must be belt-routed into the box's physical input ports (or directly into hub inputs); there is no produce-side wireless pickup. The box's output ports exist and are legally idle in this production line (an unconnected output port does not claim its front cell). Cache-slot dual-role timing behavior is throughput-scope and OUT-OF-SCOPE.
protocol_storage_box_wireless.supersedes: the pre-2026-07-18 'omni_wireless black hole' reading (zero physical ports, wireless product consumption)

slot_count_clause.adjudicated: 2026-08-06 owner (same-commodity multi-slot occupancy confirmed as a direct consequence of the cache-slot axiom; the earlier 'six different commodities' phrasing was an example, not a bound)
slot_count_clause.statement: The box's 6 cache slots are 6 INDEPENDENT single-slot groups (dynamic typing per slot; in-group exclusion vacuous; no cross-group exclusion), each group holding one cache slot of capacity 50 (parameters and provenance: cache_parameters below): one commodity per occupied slot, and the SAME commodity may occupy several slots. Whether an arriving item is accepted depends on the current type AND the remaining capacity of all 6 groups - the arrival must find an admissible non-full group, either already typed to that commodity or still free for dynamic typing. Consequently neither the number of commodity types present nor the number of already-typed groups is by itself a complete blocking test: occupied is not the same as full. For an arrival of a commodity that no group already holds with remaining capacity, the box blocks exactly when its 6 slots are all occupied, REGARDLESS of how many commodity types are involved - bounded mixed absorption with the bound stated in SLOTS, deliberately not in commodity types (owner 2026-08-06 adjudication, wording preserved verbatim). Class-(2) safety is therefore an execution invariant, not a static count: before every attempted landing at least one admissible group with remaining capacity must exist. Power coverage may be certified by predicate 6, but cache counts, arrival timing, the 10 s flush schedule, default-on state and warehouse submission success all lie outside the 6 certified predicates and must be discharged separately wherever they are relied upon. Without that invariant the box is a potentially rejecting, bounded absorber. Unpowered, the 10 s flush never runs and occupied slots never clear (power is a behavioral precondition, kernel A8).

cache_parameters.statement: Each of the 6 groups holds exactly one cache slot of capacity 50 items, so the box's static local capacity is 6 x 50 = 300 items. Landing order: an arriving item is placed in the EARLIEST admissible group in declaration order (storage_slot_1 through storage_slot_6), a group being admissible if it is empty or already typed to that commodity and not yet full. Owner 2026-08-06 in-game adjudication: fill-first holds - once a group is full the same commodity opens a further group - and the same commodity may therefore occupy several groups. Simulator rule-layer precision: the search key is declaration order, not commodity content, so a strictly earlier EMPTY group is taken in preference to a later already-typed non-full group. Within one 10 s flush cycle the two readings coincide, because the flush empties all groups together and the groups are then refilled in declaration order.
cache_parameters.provenance: Upstream simulator rule layer, IndustrialPlanner src/registry/entity-definition.ts:835-866 - createEntityDefinition({id: 'storager_1', ... storageSlotGroups: [createStorageSlotGroup('storage_slot_1', ItemDomainFlag.Solid, createSlots('slot', [50], ItemDomainFlag.Solid)), ... identically repeated through 'storage_slot_6']}); createSlots builds one slot per capacity entry (:517-526), so [50] is exactly one slot of capacity 50. Landing order: topology-compiler.ts:250-280 (one input port bound to all 6 groups yields 6 edges pushed in group declaration order) with stage-3:300-345 (each edge tried independently, a failure only continues to the next), pinned by regression test storage-multi-slot-routing.test.ts:176-188. Snapshot IndustrialPlanner@7b946c16 (2026-08-05); verbatim line-by-line cross-check 2026-08-07 by the blind simulator cross-audit seat, archived with this batch under docs/research/canonical_batch_20260808/.
cache_parameters.evidence_grade: Owner in-game adjudication (2026-08-06) for fill-first and same-commodity multi-group occupancy; simulator rule-layer source code (not the game client) for the capacity-50 parameter and the declaration-order landing mechanism. Per the authority order in axiom_kernel.scope_premises the simulator line is supporting provenance only and can never override an owner in-game ruling.

slot_count_clause.blocking_reachability_note: Why the class-(2) blocking state is not reached on THIS production line - narrative-level and CONDITIONAL, never certified, and never a substitute for the per-arrival acceptance invariant. (a) Slot account: the box has 3 physical input ports; under the model's destination-front single-commodity exclusivity each of them carries exactly one commodity, so at most 3 commodity types reach the box. With the landing order and the 50-item slot capacity registered in cache_parameters, and with a flush cycle that starts from 6 empty groups, at most 3 groups are typed per cycle, so the 6-occupied state is not reached. This account is conditional on BOTH registered parameters and on that model face: the clause text alone bounds occupancy at 6 slots, not 3, because the same commodity may occupy several groups. Owner's 2026-08-07 adjudication reaches the same bound WITHOUT leaning on that model face: in this instance the only commodities that can reach the storage line are the 2 final products, so the sole theoretical route to 6 occupied groups - a mixed belt carrying 7 or more kinds inside one 10 s window - cannot be assembled at all. (b) Item-count account: 3 input ports x 1 item per 2 s tick x the 10 s flush period give at most 15 arrivals per cycle. That arrival rate is unconditional, but the step that calls it far below the cache is a comparison against the 300-item static capacity and therefore also depends on the registered capacity parameter. Neither account is a certified predicate - rate and timing are OUT-OF-SCOPE (PROJECT_LOCK.md 1A B) - and neither discharges the acceptance invariant for a general layout; they explain only why it holds on the frozen production line. Status: leg (a) as stated here is a CURRENT-MODEL theorem, not an assertion about adjudicated game semantics - per model_stricter_faces_usage_rule it names its dependency on registered face (1) and is invalidated for re-proof if that face is unlocked; the owner leg above and leg (b) do not carry that dependency. The instance-level consequence is recorded in mixed_commodity_flow.terminal_clause. Standing ledger entry: this is the reachability audit demanded before any use of the class label.

power_source_note.statement: The hub (protocol core) IS the base's power source; power poles draw from the hub unconditionally at any distance and re-broadcast coverage; the hub itself has no coverage range and needs no power; generators live in another base (power budget externalized). The modeled predicate 'a powered facility must be covered by some pole stencil' is therefore effect-equivalent to game mechanics (the mandatory hub makes every pole powered), and no wiring/link constraint is modeled for poles.

See semantics.axiom_kernel.

item_admission_port_exclusion.statement: The 1x1 item admission port exists in game v1.1 but is deliberately not modeled. For a fixed already-separated route, its occupied cell is geometrically equivalent to a straight belt (any cell that admits it admits a straight belt) and its quota/rate behavior remains outside the 6 certified predicates. Its item-filtering behavior can nevertheless change the operational safety of a mixed route. The present materials do not provide a certificate-level without-loss-of-generality proof that omission preserves the full adjudicated-game feasible domain or full-game lex optimum, because the rate lemma is conditional and its allocation preconditions are not certified. Until an independent completeness transformation is supplied, omission of the admission port is an explicit certification-scope restriction rather than an unconditional safe-exclusion theorem.
item_admission_port_exclusion.authority: Safe-exclusion argument, now explicitly CONDITIONAL. As of this batch no candidate pool and no predicate of the released model consumes the admission port, so the exclusion still stands on the released model - but that is a contingent state, not a standing authority. Any predicate that forbids what only a filtering admission port could realize WOULD consume it; the de-mix prohibition proposed on the mixflow line (two commodities merging and later splitting) is exactly such a predicate - it lives on branch mixflow-surgery (commit fb76e15, routing_subproblem._add_demix_ban_constraints) and is NOT merged into the released model as of 2026-08-07. If any batch lands such a predicate, this authority lapses on landing and the exclusion must be re-adjudicated together with the statement above. Owner disposition 2026-08-07: leave the exclusion in place for now, carried as the explicit certification-scope restriction stated above; modeling the 1x1 filter cell is NOT undertaken by this batch.

rationale_restated.statement: Geometric equivalence and the out-of-scope status of the admission port's quota/rate behavior remain established. The stronger claim that sorting is never structurally required is not established for all legal layouts by the current rate lemma. Inside a layout that separately discharges every rate_lemma_scope precondition, intermediate pure flow and class-(1) terminal absorption may make an admission port unnecessary; outside that allocation profile this entry asserts no such result. The sorting-terminal theorem remains a necessary condition on any sorting construction, not a proof that every sorting construction can be removed. Certification therefore excludes admission-port filtering by declared scope unless a separate layout-preserving replacement proof is archived.

rate_lemma_scope.statement: Scope declaration for the intermediate pure-flow arithmetic lemma. This is a theorem about one explicitly stated rate-allocation profile, not a theorem over all legal layouts and not a certified predicate. Preconditions: (i) full production at the frozen production_targets, namely 3.0 valley_battery and 2.75 qiaoyu_capsule equivalent-full-speed lines; (ii) equal inter-machine duty allocation. Precondition (ii) has a FACT half and an ASSUMPTION half, and only the second is imposed here. Fact half (a property of the frozen instance set, not a restriction introduced by this lemma): for each operation o with exact aggregate machine-run demand R_o, the frozen mandatory instance set already contains exactly n_o = ceil(R_o) machines carrying o - verified for all 17 operations across the 266 = 219 + 46 + 1 instances. Assumption half: every one of those n_o machines runs at the same utilization u_o = R_o / n_o. (iii) no lane dilution: each per-machine commodity stream of rate r uses exactly ceil(r / C) occupied belt lanes, where C = 1 item per tick is the lane capacity. Under (i)-(iii), r - (ceil(r / C) - 1)C is a lower bound on the least-loaded lane of that stream. For intermediate commodities the resulting residual set, including full lanes, is {5/6, 11/12, 19/22, 21/22, 10/11, 1}; every pair of non-full intermediate residual lower bounds sums to more than C. Therefore no two intermediate commodities can share one lane within this allocation profile. The 21/22 value occurs on sandleaf input-side feeds. Final-product outputs are excluded from the intermediate pair test. Unequal inter-machine duty allocation, including staircase allocation, or the use of additional lanes beyond ceil(r / C), leaves this precondition family and the lemma asserts nothing about that layout.
rate_lemma_scope.usage_rule: The 6 certified predicates do not record inter-machine duty allocation, actual lane count, lane occupancy or commodity rate. A certificate therefore does NOT discharge preconditions (ii) or (iii). A certification narrative may use this lemma only when it supplies a separate, auditable witness or proof for every precondition on the particular layout being discussed. Without that additional discharge, use of the lemma for a full-layout, without-loss-of-generality, admission-port-necessity or expressiveness-gap claim is prohibited. A post-hoc external proof may discharge the preconditions; the ordinary CERTIFIED result alone cannot. Rate arithmetic never enters a certificate (PROJECT_LOCK.md 1A B unchanged).
rate_lemma_scope.recompute_scope: The supplied script evaluates one representative per-operation commodity stream under equal inter-machine duty allocation and minimal lane count. It iterates both recipe input and output sides. The 21/22 residual occurs on two sandleaf input-side records. Full lanes with residual 1 are omitted from the printed residual list because they cannot participate in a <=1 violation; the intermediate set containing 1 is therefore a derived set, not the literal stdout set. Terminal commodities are removed only for the pair test. The script does not enumerate physical routing lanes and does not verify the separate '2-4 terminal lanes' quantity. Machine-verified record carried over from the superseded statement text (2026-08-06 recompute): pairwise-sum <= 1 counterexamples over intermediate residual lanes = 0, and the full-rate recipe share was corrected to 10/17 - an earlier 9/17 was a transcription error.
rate_lemma_scope.weaker_precondition_note: ARCHIVAL NOTE, not a precondition of the lemma above. A strictly weaker structural precondition also suffices provided (iii) is kept: every machine actually carrying an operation runs at utilization u > 5/6, and every per-machine commodity stream still uses only ceil(rate) lanes. In the frozen recipes an intermediate commodity's full-speed rate coefficient per machine can only be k in {1, 2, 3}, giving least-loaded-lane lower bounds u > 5/6 for k=1, 2u-1 > 2/3 for k=2 and 3u-2 > 1/2 for k=3 - all above 1/2, so any two intermediate residual lanes still sum to more than one lane capacity. Independently recomputed 2026-08-07: the non-equal allocations [1, 9/10 x5] for 11/2 over 6 machines, [1, 19/20 x10] for 21/2 over 11 machines and [1, 7/8, 7/8] for 11/4 over 3 machines each meet total demand with every machine above 5/6, which shows this precondition is strictly weaker than equal duty. It is recorded as an archival alternative only: it still needs (iii), it is harder to audit than equal duty, and the certificate discharges neither. The still more general sufficient condition - every non-full intermediate lane carries strictly more than 1/2 - has no certificate variable that could witness it.

port_commodity_scope.statement: The binding model is slot-single-commodity: every port slot carries exactly one commodity. Adjudicated game semantics allow a wired warehouse-line input port to absorb several commodities at once (mixed_commodity_flow.terminal_clause, class 1), which the model cannot express - 'one core port eating two final products' has no encoding. The supplied recompute quantifies this expressiveness gap as 2-4 final-product lanes only inside the allocation profile stated in semantics.rate_lemma_scope and only after all of its preconditions are separately discharged. The ordinary certificate does not establish that profile, so outside it this entry does not bound the size or commodity scope of the gap. Certification remains explicitly scoped to the game fragment in which every wired warehouse-line input port carries a single commodity, unless an independent completeness proof is supplied. This entry exists so the gap cannot silently be read as full generality.
port_commodity_scope.axiom_derivation: kernel A11 (commodity identity via player-configured warehouse links; binding one-commodity generic_output per boundary port is its mirror) + A4 (wired warehouse input side = protocol core alone). See semantics.axiom_kernel.
